title: JUnit and Parameterized Tests
summary: Use focused assertions, independent setup and parameterized input cases.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: JUnit Testing in Spring Boot | @Test @ParameterizedTest @CsvSource @ArgumentsSource @SpringBootTest

richText: JUnit Jupiter runs the test method
JUnit Jupiter is the JUnit 5 programming model. @Test marks a test method. Assertions compare the expected result with the actual result. A failed assertion fails the test.
Use spring-boot-starter-test in test scope for the Boot-managed testing dependencies. A plain Jupiter test does not need @SpringBootTest.
Structure a test as arrange, act and assert. Prepare input, call the behavior, then check a result. Give the method a name that describes the rule being checked.
Use assertEquals(expected, actual), assertTrue for a boolean rule, and assertThrows for an expected failure. A not-null assertion does not prove that fields or permissions are correct.
Run one rule with several inputs
@ParameterizedTest runs the same method once for each argument set. @CsvSource suits short rows containing simple values. Each row maps to the method parameters.
This example checks a real input rule. Titles must contain at least one non-whitespace character. A row that only repeats the implementation would give weak evidence.
@ValueSource supplies one value per invocation. @ArgumentsSource delegates argument creation to an ArgumentsProvider. Use it for objects or reusable datasets that are awkward to express as CSV.
ArgumentsProvider returns a stream of Arguments. JUnit calls the provider and invokes the test for each returned argument set. Use fresh mutable objects if the test changes its input.
@BeforeEach runs before every invocation. Use it to prepare independent state. @AfterEach releases resources. @BeforeAll and @AfterAll handle class-level setup and cleanup.

@Disabled skips a test. A skipped test proves no behavior. In the tutorial repository, several sample service tests are disabled. Their presence is not evidence that the application passes those checks.
Use @SpringBootTest only when Spring wiring is part of the requirement. An ordinary rule test should construct the class directly.

Check boundary cases deliberately. For journal ownership, include the owner, another user and a missing entry. For title rules, include normal text, whitespace and null. These cases exercise different paths.
